stem: A 4-year-old girl is brought in by her father, who works as a hospital orderly, after about three weeks of cough and reduced energy. She has never been treated for TB before. A gastric aspirate was sent for molecular testing and was positive for M. tuberculosis with rifampicin resistance detected; follow-up testing confirmed isoniazid and fluoroquinolone susceptibility (rifampicin mono-resistant TB), with no other risk factors for resistance beyond this result -- no HIV, no prior treatment. She lives with her 10-year-old brother, who is asymptomatic on screening. Exam (patient): mild wasting, right-sided crackles, no lymphadenopathy.

patient.occupation: not applicable (household occupational context: father works as a hospital orderly)
patient.social_history: Lives with parents and her 10-year-old brother
patient.presenting_complaint: Cough and reduced energy, confirmed rifampicin mono-resistant TB
patient.exam_findings: Mild wasting, right-sided crackles, no lymphadenopathy
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: The patient's presentation assumed low-risk for resistant TB given her young age and absence of prior treatment, arguing against confirmatory resistance testing
Her brother's lack of current symptoms taken as sufficient reassurance without considering preventive treatment
ntep_correct_actions: Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.

Offer her brother, a household contact of her fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR/RR-TB, a fixed, standardized preventive regimen of 6 months of daily levofloxacin as a routine part of programmatic TB preventive treatment, once active TB disease is excluded in him.
who_correct_actions: Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.

Offer her brother, a household contact of her fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR/RR-TB, a fixed, standardized preventive regimen of 6 months of daily levofloxacin as a routine part of programmatic TB preventive treatment, once active TB disease is excluded in him.
us_correct_actions: Reserve rapid rifampicin-resistance testing for patients who meet at least one specific risk criterion (prior TB treatment, birth in or residence in a higher-TB-incidence country, contact with a known MDR-TB case, or HIV infection); do not order it routinely for a patient with none of these risk factors.

Treat offering preventive treatment to her brother as only conditionally appropriate versus observation alone; if treatment is given, individualize the regimen and duration to her (the source case's) susceptibility pattern rather than using a fixed levofloxacin regimen.
critical_error_conditions: Omitting rifampicin-resistance/confirmatory testing given this child's TB diagnosis
Concluding that no preventive action is warranted for her brother because he is currently asymptomatic
expected_divergence_points: Whether rifampicin-resistance testing is performed universally or only for patients meeting specific US risk criteria
Whether household contacts of fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR/RR-TB receive a fixed, standardized preventive regimen or an individualized regimen contingent on a conditional decision to treat
